lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Soften: "This proves every family must agree."

FEEDBACK
This suggests some families may agree — if the evidence shows that.

CHECK
Strong modality on weak evidence misleads readers.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Rewrite eight absolute claims into balanced modality. Label certainty and justify two choices.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Balanced language uses careful modality (might, may, suggests) when evidence is partial and avoids absolute always/never without proof.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Rewrite eight absolute claims into balanced modality. Label certainty and justify two choices. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: This suggests some families may agree — if the evidence shows that. Reasoning: I used modality by attending to balanced rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Strong modality on weak evidence misleads readers. Correction: This suggests some families may agree — if the evidence shows that. Why: the correction restores accurate use of modality.

Parent: Likely misconception: Strong modality on weak evidence misleads readers. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating modality on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with modality, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
"The survey suggests some students want longer recess" is balanced; "Everyone hates short recess forever" is not.

TRY FIRST
Soften: "This proves every family must agree."

FEEDBACK
This suggests some families may agree — if the evidence shows that.
teach_steps.explain:
Balanced language uses careful modality (might, may, suggests) when evidence is partial and avoids absolute always/never without proof.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
